title: Fix the Assignment Instead of Comparison
description: The program should check if a number equals 5 and print a message.
expectedBehavior: The program should print 'x is five' when x equals 5.
actualProblem: if (x = 5) attempts to assign 5 to x inside the condition. Since the result of that assignment is an int, not a boolean, Java refuses to compile it: 'incompatible types: int cannot be converted to boolean'.
explanation: Java's if statement requires a boolean expression. Unlike some languages, an assignment (int result) can never silently pass as a condition, which is exactly why this typo is caught at compile time rather than causing a subtle logic bug.
